en.title: Jobs and workplaces
en.summary: Talking about your work now and before, with the past simple, the passive and the present simple.

paragraphs: People often ask what you do and where you work. To answer well you need the present tense for what you do every day, the past tense for your earlier jobs, and sometimes the passive for the place itself. Hana's story uses all three.

My name is Hana and I work in a hospital. I am a nurse. Before this job I worked in a pharmacy for three years. I studied at university in Leeds and finished my studies in 2019. The hospital is very large. It was built in 1965, and it was repaired two years ago. Every day I start work at seven o'clock. I check the patients and I help the doctors. After a night shift I am tired, but I like my job because I help people.

**1. The past simple tells a finished story.** Regular verbs add -ed to the base form: worked, finished. If the verb ends in a consonant and y, change y to ied: study becomes studied. Many common verbs are irregular and must be learned one by one: be becomes was or were, and go becomes went. See Introduction to Grammar: Past tenses and aspect.

**2. The passive hides the doer.** Use be and the past participle when the doer is not important or not known. In the text, the person who built the hospital does not matter, so we say **It was built in 1965.** To say who did it, add by: **It was built by a local company.** See Introduction to Grammar: Voice, reflexive and impersonal verbs.

paragraphs: **3. The present simple is for habits.** Every day I start work at seven is something Hana does again and again. With he, she or it the verb takes -s: **She starts work at seven.** See Introduction to Grammar: Present tense, being and having.

items: A job takes an article: **I am a nurse**, not I am nurse.
Job is a thing you can count and work is not. Say **I have a good job** and **I have a lot of work**.
You work **in** a hospital or a shop, **at** a bank or a university, and **for** a company.

paragraphs: In the United Kingdom the National Health Service, the NHS, gives free medical care to people who live there. It is one of the largest employers in the country, and nurses, doctors and many other workers come from all over the world.
